course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Global Conflict
unit.description: Study how empires collapsed, why two world wars were fought and how they were conducted, how the Depression reshaped economies, and how mass atrocities happened.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.8 key concept: during the twentieth century, governments carried out genocide and mass atrocities, including the Holocaust
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the Holocaust, 1933–1945
stimulusBlocks.text:
The Nazi regime first stripped German Jews of their rights. The Nuremberg Laws of 1935 took away their citizenship and banned marriage between Jews and other Germans. After the invasion of the Soviet Union in 1941, mobile killing units shot hundreds of thousands of Jews.

In January 1942, Nazi officials met at Wannsee to coordinate the systematic murder of Europe's Jews. About six million Jews were killed, many in death camps such as Auschwitz. The Nazis also murdered Roma, disabled people, and others they considered inferior.

questions.prompt: The passage best illustrates which pattern?
choices: Persecution escalated from legal discrimination to mass murder

Jews in Germany gained rights after 1935
Persecution of Jews began only after the war ended in 1945
questions.explanation: Laws in 1935 led, in wartime, to organized killing.
choiceExplanations: Laws in 1935 led, in wartime, to organized killing.
It escalated.
They lost rights.
It began in the 1930s.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.8 key concept: mass atrocities in the twentieth century included the Armenian genocide, the Cambodian genocide, and the Rwandan genocide
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing several twentieth-century genocides
stimulusBlocks.text:
During World War I, the Ottoman government deported and killed a large share of its Armenian population, beginning in 1915. In Cambodia, the Khmer Rouge regime emptied the cities and forced people into rural labor from 1975 to 1979; between 1.5 and 2 million people died. In Rwanda in 1994, Hutu extremists killed an estimated 500,000 to 800,000 people, mostly Tutsi, in about one hundred days.

In each case, the killers used propaganda that described the victims as enemies of the nation.

questions.explanation: The passage says the killers described victims as enemies of the nation.
choiceExplanations: Propaganda played a role.
The passage says the killers described victims as enemies of the nation.
Propaganda shows planning.
They occurred in Asia, Africa, and the Middle East.
questions.distinguisher: The passage says killers used propaganda in each case.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.8 key concept: Nazi Germany carried out the Holocaust, the systematic murder of European Jews
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the Holocaust, 1933–1945
stimulusBlocks.text:
After the Nazi Party took power in Germany in 1933, the government excluded Jews from public life. The Nuremberg Laws of 1935 stripped German Jews of citizenship, and the violence of Kristallnacht in November 1938 destroyed synagogues and Jewish businesses. After Germany invaded the Soviet Union in 1941, special units shot hundreds of thousands of Jews, and in 1942 Nazi officials met at Wannsee, near Berlin, to coordinate the murder of all European Jews.

Millions were deported to killing centers such as Auschwitz-Birkenau, where gas chambers were used. About six million Jews died. The Nazis also murdered Roma, people with disabilities, Polish and Soviet civilians, and political opponents.

questions.prompt: The German invasion of the Soviet Union in 1941 contributed to the Holocaust by
choices: ending all persecution of Jews living inside Germany
making Germany an ally of the Soviet Union in the war
removing Germany's authority over occupied Poland and France
opening the way to mass shootings by special units
questions.explanation: After the invasion, special units followed the army and shot large numbers of Jews.
choiceExplanations: Persecution did not end.
Germany and the Soviet Union were at war.
Germany still controlled occupied Poland.
After the invasion, special units followed the army and shot large numbers of Jews.
questions.distinguisher: Germany had signed a pact with the Soviet Union in 1939, but the 1941 invasion ended it.
